thumbnail.analysis: Actual 1280x720 and 320x180 inspected. White field; left a kneeling cartoon man in a gray hoodie with a shocked open mouth pulls open a steel safe that is empty except for one glowing orange coin and a curling receipt; right heavy black "30 AND / BROKE?" with a curved arrow to the safe. Mobile: two-line text and empty safe read immediately. Image promises a personal diagnosis ("are you broke at 30?") and emptiness; script supports debt/low-savings framing but is a statistics tour plus composite stories rather than a test the viewer can take. Consistent negative emotional promise with title.

script.analysis: All 20,080 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: 3 a.m. banking-app anxiety, roommate-bought-a-house comparison, joke about savings lasting 12 minutes; early subscribe/like CTA. Sections: student loans (average $42K, $436 payment, IDR negative amortization, composite "Michael"), credit-score drops after delinquency reporting, credit cards (average $4K at 22%, composite "Sarah" with itemized $3,800 balance), housing (under-35 ownership 37%, $500K average price, 6.7% 2024 rate, affordability ratios), rental screening, savings (1x salary by 30, $1,000 emergency stat, "median" $62,400), $800/month retirement advice paradox, Fidelity 1x benchmark, $14K average balance and 4% rule, closing "economic hellscape" reassurance. Strong empathetic framing ("not about discipline") is consistent throughout, but the script contains no remedies and several numeric inconsistencies. Composite stories are labeled "real situation that represents millions" without verification. ASR fillers and fragments ("Dart,", "soulc crushingly") retained; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 Michael: $68,500 at ~6.5% over 10 years gives ~$778/month, matching $780, but $780 x 12 / $75,000 = 12.5% of gross, not "over 15%". A $420 payment on $65,000 covers monthly interest at the 6.08% (~$329) or 7.08% (~$384) graduate rates of recent years; balance growth to $68,500 requires a rate near 7.75% or a lower payment, so the story is internally doubtful. Average $42K student debt "for 30-year-olds" and $436 payment unsourced; the credit-score drop (100+ points, 177-point average for 720+) resembles 2025 NY Fed reporting but was not verified here.

7000:14000 $4,000 at 22% = $880/year, consistent. Sarah 1,500 + 800 + 1,500 = $3,800, correct. A fixed $120/month at 22% repays $3,800 in ~48 months with ~$1,940 interest; "over 18 years and more than $8,000" only follows if the minimum shrinks with the balance, unstated. $380 + $120 = $500 = ~13% of $3,800 take-home, not "roughly 10%".

7000:14000 Under-35 ownership ~37% is an under-35 figure; "nearly 2/3 of 30-year-olds renting" generalizes to a narrower age with higher ownership. Average price over $500K is an average (medians are lower). $400K loan at 6.7% for 30 years = ~$2,581/month, not ~$2,400; 2,400/3,800 = 63% as stated. 28% x $58,000 / 12 = ~$1,353, correct. Claim that rent is "often higher than mortgage payments" contradicts the script's own $1,800-2,000 rent versus $2,400+ mortgage.

14000:20080 Fidelity 1x salary by 30 benchmark correctly attributed. "More than half can't cover $1,000" resembles Bankrate-style all-adult survey results, then is restated as "Americans your age" - age conflation. "$62,400 median savings" matches the 2022 SCF mean transaction-account balance (~$62,410), not a median. $800/month = 21% of $3,800, not 25%. $14,000 x 4% = $560/year = ~$46.67/month, correct arithmetic; the $14K "average" for 30s unsourced. "Only 14% have $100K saved" unsourced.
